notes: Bank: 18 of 35 newly solved (11 still none, 6 still wrong, all for the reasons listed); --regress: 355 tasks, BROKEN 0. No pack operator appears in a wrong final program. Robustness checks in scratch_r4_strings/: every solved task still solves when each of its other asserts is used as the visible example (35/35 variants), and 17/17 reworded descriptions solve. Risks: (1) The only solved regression task whose program changed is MbppX/542 (a0.replace(' ', ':') -> re.sub(r'[ ,.]', ':', a0)); it still passes and now matches its reference. (2) upper_then_lower_r4s follows the bank references' anchored [A-Z]+[a-z]+$, and lower_underscore_lower_r4s allows exactly one underscore. A held-out reference that searches anywhere, or allows several underscores, would differ on some strings. (3) words_of_k_chars_r4s (9 rules) are gated on a lead word before the number ('all five characters', 'of five letters', 'five-letter'), so lists like 'three, four, five characters' and 'at least four characters' do not name them; the scratch negative test confirms the list case. (4) The a/b regex rules have the letters a and b fixed, as the exercises do. I deliberately added no other quantifier variants (e.g. 'two to three b'), because none is in my bank. Engine observations: ends_with/2 is retired in the manifest, so 879 is solved by a fixed-letter rule. Equal bool values merge at level 1 and the first named predicate keeps the slot, whatever its keyword specificity, so pack load order decides when two packs' predicates are named by one description and agree on the example; letting specificity re-label the slot would make this order-independent. Most of the remaining failures answer with task-specific words ('Not Possible', 'Accept'/'Discard', 'Valid IP address'). The visible example shows only one of each pair, so no rule can supply the other. Reading number words followed by a unit ('five characters') as constants would let the core of_length replace my number-word family.
